title: Mini-coalescer with hysteresis and kernel-profile routing to stabilize embedding p99
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We see intermittent p99 spikes on the embeddings endpoint for short (<=32 token) queries during bursty traffic. Current micro-batch coalescer oscillates between aggressive coalescing and immediate dispatch, causing tail amplification and unfairness across priorities. Additionally, the kernel selection heuristic does not account for transient sequence-length skew at the batch level, leading to suboptimal kernel choices and added latency for mixed-length batches.

Goal: Reduce embedding p99 by at least 30% for typical short-query workloads while preserving throughput and avoiding increased average latency. Do this by implementing a lightweight mini-coalescer with hysteresis to avoid oscillation and a kernel-profile-aware routing rule that chooses kernels based on short-window batch sequence distribution.

Proposed approach:
1) Mini-coalescer: introduce a short, configurable hold window (e.g., 2-6ms) that groups arrivals into micro-coalesced dispatches when beneficial. Use hysteresis counters to prevent rapid toggling in bursty scenarios. Ensure cost model accounts for marginal queuing vs batching savings.
2) Kernel-profile routing: collect per-mini-batch sequence-length histogram (short/medium/long) and route to the kernel optimized for the majority profile; if mixed, prefer low-latency kernel or fallback to slow-path with early-exit heuristics.
3) Prioritization: integrate with existing priority stacks so low-latency prefetched/priority requests can preempt coalescing when required.
4) Telemetry & evaluation: add micro-batch level metrics (hold_time, batch_size, sequence_histogram, kernel_choice) and synthetic tail-testing harness to replay production arrival patterns.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: global scheduler rewrite, quantization changes, or model-level architecture tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Embedding p99 reduced by >=30% for short (<=32 token) synthetic workload compared to baseline A (measured across 1M requests)
No regression in median latency (>5% increase) for mixed-length workloads
Batching telemetry emitted for each dispatch (hold_time, batch_size, sequence_histogram, kernel_choice)
Config flags to disable mini-coalescer and to tune hysteresis/hold window
Benchmarked on dedicated staging cluster and PR with unit + integration tests merged
comments: 2026-02-10 Miguel Soto: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded to Drive (drive:redwood/embeddings/minicoalescer/kickoff). Agreed to implement simplest hysteresis counter first and iterate.
2026-02-18 Aisha Kapoor: Initial microbench harness committed (github:redwood/infra/emb-harness PR#112). Early results show p99 reduction ~18% on steady traffic but oscillation on bursty traces.
2026-02-25 Miguel Soto: Added per-mini-batch seq-length histogram to telemetry. Observed mixed-length batches caused 25-40ms kernel overhead when routed to generic kernel.
2026-03-02 Eng review: Design doc posted (confluence:redwood/embeddings/minicoalescer-design). Design feedback: add backpressure safety limits and a per-tenant opt-out flag.
2026-03-05 QA: Synthetic burst trace replay added; found worst-case oscillation when hold window <3ms. Increasing hysteresis counter helped stabilize dispatching.
2026-03-09 Miguel Soto: Prototype merged to feature branch (github:redwood/runtime PR#1458). Running staged ab tests against canary pool for 48h.

2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Canary metrics after 24h: short-query p99 down 29% (close to target), median unchanged. Some tenants with very high variance saw no wins; follow-up to add tenant-configurable thresholds.
Next steps: finish per-tenant config UI in console, run 7-day canary, and prepare release notes for runtime-1.24
